Multiscale Divergence Index

R code to measure residential segregation at several spatial scales with the spatial Divergence Index (Roberto 2015), on a 100 m population grid.

Groups: born in Sweden (sb), born in Europe (fb_e), born outside Europe (fb_ne).

Method

For every populated 100 m cell in the study area (municipality code 180), the group counts of all cells whose centre lies within a radius of 150, 300, 600 or 1000 m are summed; the cell itself is included, and cells in a 10 km buffer around the study area count as neighbours. The local Divergence Index is

DI = Σ pg · log(pg / rg)

where pg is a group’s share of the local population and rg its share in the whole study area. The overall DI at each radius is the mean of local DI weighted by each cell’s population.

Data

The analysis was developed on Swedish register data for Stockholm (2022), aggregated to 100 m cells. Those data cannot be shared, so this repository contains simulated data for a fictional city instead (data/simulated_grid_2022.csv, made by simulate_grid_data.R). The simulated grid has the same columns as the real one and was calibrated only to city-wide aggregates (number of cells, persons per cell, group shares, DI by radius). All results below are for the simulated city, not for Stockholm.

Reproducing

  1. Run simulate_grid_data.R to create data/simulated_grid_2022.csv.
  2. Run divergence_multiscale.R with in_file set to that file. Results and figures are written to results/.

Packages: dplyr, tidyr, readr, ggplot2.

Reference

Roberto, E. (2015). The Divergence Index: A decomposable measure of segregation and inequality. arXiv:1508.01167
